# Verified implementation context

Assess supported behavior against the contracts and implementation below. Report
concrete defects; conditional claims must establish a reachable production path.
This context supplies code that may otherwise fall into a different diff chunk.
It does not waive concurrency, cancellation, correctness or security checks.

The native driver deliberately supports one native main loop per process.
Driver.Run gates entry with processRun.CompareAndSwap(false, true); once started,
it never resets that flag. A second application/native run is explicitly rejected
and documented in specs/windows-services.md. The package-global native callbacks
therefore stop permanently at native shutdown. Headless native callback unit tests
isolate/reset this state through withMenuCommitState(t); a second native run is
not supported and is not a lifecycle bug to require resetting stopped for.

Native menu callbacks store *platformServices. nativeMenuAction calls its
invokeMenu method. That method ONLY enqueues via Application.Post; it does not
execute user code on the Cocoa main thread. The command executes later when the
application UI owner drains the queue. The code in services.go is:

func (s *platformServices) invokeMenu(id string) {
    err := s.owner.Post(func() {
        if s.commands == nil { return }
        if err := s.commands.Invoke(s.owner.Context(), id); err != nil && s.onError != nil { s.onError(err) }
        s.owner.Invalidate("")
    })
    if err != nil && s.onError != nil {
        go func() { s.owner.Do(func() { s.onError(err) }) }()
    }
}

Services are explicitly worker-only outside Do/Drain/View/widget callbacks;
commands needing clipboard or file panels must launch a worker. This avoids
blocking either the native main loop or the owner. The menu commit tests use a
real app+registry and verify zero command invocations until Drain, then exactly
one. nativeMenuAction therefore has a type-enforced enqueue path, rather than
accepting an arbitrary synchronous user callback.

reconcile.go attaches and orders the COMPLETE desired tree before calling syncRecord(next.r,n). syncRecord in driver.go visits parents before descendants, setting syncSemantics on each parent before recursively syncing its children. Thus syncControl computes its final disabled snapshot after topology reparenting and ancestor property updates. Its initial mount snapshot is overwritten by that final sync. TestDisabledSnapshotAfterReparentAndAncestorUpdate explicitly queues an edit before moving a retained field into a disabled ancestor, then proves delivery is rejected; it then enables the ancestor without changing the child and proves the new edit is accepted. Inspect a reachable path before reporting a speculative pre-attachment snapshot bug.
